newsitem.title: USA: Corning has loss in quarter.
newsitem.headline: Corning has loss in quarter.

text.p: Corning Inc., which is spinning off its health care business, Tuesday reported a net loss of $19.8 million for the third quarter, hurt by a stiff government fine related to a guilty plea for Medicare fraud.
The quarterly loss, equal to 9 cents a share, compared with a net profit of $83.5 million, or 37 cents a share, in the 1995 period.

Profits from continuing operations, excluding a $115 million charge related to the government fine, were $95.2 million, or 42 cents a share, compared with $101.1 million, or 45 cents a share, in the year-ago period.
The results from continuing operations were a shade better than forecasts and Corning's stock rose 50 cents to $39.25 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
Analysts had forecast that Corning would earn 41 cents a share on average from ongoing operations, according to First Call, which tracks estimates.
Sales fell 13 percent in the quarter to $910.2 million from $1.05 billion.
Corning, which on May 14 announced the plan to spin off its health care businesses, said Tuesday that it was on track to complete the transaction by year-end.
Splitting its clinical laboratories and pharmaceutical services businesses into a separate company will shrink Corning's $5.3 billion in annual revenue by about $2 billion.
Corning is spinning off the units to focus on its ceramic, speciality glass and optical electric fiber businesses.

The company took the $115 charge after it agreed last week to plead guilty to conspiracy to defraud the government and pay $119 million in penalties and fines on behalf of its Damon clinical laboratory unit, which it acquired in 1993.

Damon submitted millions of fraudulent claims for payment for bogus lab tests in 1993 and 1994, federal prosecutor Donald Stern said in announcing the fine last Wednesday. He said Corning has cooperated with the government's ongoing investigation.
